headline: High: shared-memory and file-based interaction can leak support data and create cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared content channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes files like CLAUDE.md, while cognee operates on documents and session memory. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if caveman ingests cognee-produced text or shared files. The pair lacks direct documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF caveman reads cognee-generated documents or notes as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic instruction parsing from shared files
Add a provenance header to all inter-agent handoffs
Review any shared note before execution
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; cognee touches customer support data, personal data, and finance data. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive data can flow from B into A's outputs or logs. The profiles do not show default isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or document store
IF support or finance data is copied into caveman-readable notes
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared folders
Restrict caveman to redacted inputs only
Turn on tenant isolation in cognee
Audit logs for copied personal or finance data
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and caveman can use MCP while cognee runs as a CLI with session memory. If they target the same mutable workspace or graph-backed state, concurrent writes can overwrite each other. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory or memory store
IF the orchestrator does not provide file or record locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations manually
Use read-only mode for one agent
Snapshot state before each run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If cognee treats caveman output as authoritative, an error can propagate into downstream workflows. The pair has no documented verification step, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF cognee ingests caveman-generated notes without human review
IF downstream workflows execute based on unverified summaries
mitigations: Require human review before ingestion
Mark generated notes as untrusted
Compare outputs against source documents
Limit downstream actions to suggestions only
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while caveman touches session logs and memory files. If those data classes are moved into caveman-managed files or logs, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF personal or finance data is written into caveman logs or notes
IF retention policies differ between the two storage paths
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of caveman artifacts
Apply a shared retention policy
Redact personal data before transfer
Document data residency for both systems
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across storage paths
